nodes.name: One-pot synthesis of Pt_tet @ Ni(OH)2
nodes.procedure: In a 30 ml glass vial, 20 mg Pt(acac)2, 25.6 mg Ni(acac)2, 32 mg W(CO)6 and 135 mg glucose were dissolved in a mixture of 3 ml oleylamine and 2 ml octadecene. The mixture was sonicated for 1 h, and the resulting homogeneous solution was kept at 80 °C for 2.5 h and then heated to 140 °C for another 8 h. After the reaction, the precipitate was centrifuged out at 20,130g and washed by ethanol/hexane (25 ml/5 ml) three times. The final product was suspended in 10 ml cyclohexane.

nodes.name: Carbon black loading and annealing
nodes.procedure: In a 30 ml glass vial, 30 mg carbon black (the carbon black was annealed under Ar at 200 °C for 1 h before use) was sonicated in 15 ml ethanol for 1 h. Five millilitres Pt_tet @ Ni(OH)2 hexane solution was then added into the carbon black/ethanol solution, and the mixture was sonicated for another 1 h. The catalysts were centrifuged out at 20,130g and washed with cyclohexane/ethanol solution three times, followed by drying in a vacuum oven for 1 h. The Pt_tet @ Ni(OH)2/C were then annealed in the air at 200 °C for 2 h to fully remove the surface remaining ligands.

nodes.procedure: The crystalline Ni(OH)2 nanoplates were synthesized via adding 0.5 ml 30 wt% ammonia water drop by drop into 100 ml Ni(NO3)2 solution (10 g L^-1) with 0.25 g cetyltrimethyl ammonium bromide (CTAB) as the surfactant.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Pt assigned to Pt(0) with minor Pt(II) species, Ni species mainly Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy studies show that Pt can be assigned to Pt(0) with minor Pt(II) species, while the Ni species are mainly Ni(OH)₂ (Supplementary Fig. 5)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD reveals face-centred cubic Pt crystalline structure with no apparent diffraction peaks for Ni species, consistent with amorphous Ni(OH)₂ shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction studies reveal face-centred cubic Pt crystalline structure (Supplementary Fig. 5), with no apparent diffraction peaks for Ni species, consistent with the amorphous nature of the Ni(OH)₂ shell

properties.description: 3D molecular crystal structure with coordination polyhedra

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge EXAFS shows major Ni-O peak at 1.66 Å and Ni-Ni peak at 2.69 Å with lower intensity and broader width than crystalline α-Ni(OH)₂, confirming amorphous nature; Ni-Pt coordination at 3.10 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) signal of Pt_tet @ Ni(OH)₂ exhibits a major peak of Ni-O at 1.66 Å, and a second major peak of Ni-Ni at 2.69 Å ... The best-fitting results show that the bonding distance of Ni–Pt coordination (3.10 Å)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge and Pt L₃-edge XANES suggest Ni oxidation state slightly lower than +2, Pt slightly higher than 0, indicating partial charge transfer from Pt to Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Ni K-edge and Pt L₃-edge suggest that the oxidation state of Ni is slightly lower than +2, while that of Pt is slightly higher than 0

nodes.characterization_summary: CV reveals proton-accessible ECSA of Pt_tet@Ni(OH)₂ is ~80% of naked Pt_tet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the cyclic voltammetry (CV) studies reveal that the Pt_tet @ Ni(OH)₂ displays an ECSA about 80% of the naked Pt_tet (Fig. 3a)
